modern.name: Scroll-driven animations
modern.description: The animation-timeline, scroll-timeline, and view-timeline CSS properties advance animations based on the user's scroll position.

modern.name: random()
modern.description: The random() CSS function chooses a random numeric value within a specified range. This allows for dynamic, randomized styling using CSS.

modern.name: margin-trim
modern.description: The margin-trim CSS property removes the margins of child elements when they meet the edges of the container.

modern.name: symbols()
modern.description: The symbols() CSS function defines counter styles as a value of properties such as list-style. It's an inline alternative to the @counter-style CSS at-rule.

modern.name: text-decoration-skip-spaces
modern.description: The text-decoration-skip-spaces CSS property sets whether text decoration lines (such as underlines and overlines) skip over whitespace characters. You can use this to prevent decorations from being drawn under spaces, which is sometimes more visually appealing.

modern.name: at-rule()
modern.description: The at-rule() function, when used with @supports, checks if a CSS at-rule is supported. For example @supports at-rule(@starting-style) checks if the @starting-style at-rule is supported.

modern.name: Responsive iframes
modern.description: The frame-sizing CSS property sets the size of an <iframe> element to that of it contents, to avoid scrolling in the iframe. Embedded documents allow this with the <meta name="responsive-embedded-sizing"> element and request resizing in the embedding page by calling window.requestResize().

modern.name: alpha()
modern.description: The alpha() CSS function computes a relative color value by adjusting the opacity of an origin color.

modern.name: Anchor positioning
modern.description: Anchor positioning places an element based on the position of another element. For example, you can place a tooltip next to the content it references.

modern.name: Anchor positioning transforms
modern.description: Anchor positioned elements take CSS transforms on their anchor elements into account.

modern.name: Animation accessors
modern.description: The animation property of an AnimationEvent or TransitionEvent object is the Animation object that represents the animation (and thus the element) that fired an animation event.

modern.name: Case-sensitive attribute selector
modern.description: The s identifier in a CSS attribute selector matches attribute values case-sensitively in document languages like HTML where attribute values are case-insensitive.

modern.name: color-mix() with three or more colors
modern.description: The color-mix() CSS function accepts three or more colors.

modern.name: Customizable <select>
modern.description: The <select> element's appearance, including the button, selected option, picker dropdown, and options, can be customized using CSS.

modern.name: Heading pseudo-classes
modern.description: The :heading and :heading() CSS pseudo-classes match headings of varying levels. The :heading pseudo-class matches any heading (<h1> through <h6>). The :heading() selector matches any of the given levels. For example, :heading(1, 2) matches headings level 1 and 2.

modern.name: light-dark() image values
modern.description: The light-dark() CSS function accepts, in addition to colors, two <image> values, such as a gradient or URL, and uses one depending on the current color scheme.

modern.name: overflow-anchor
modern.description: The overflow-anchor CSS property sets an element as a possible scroll anchor, reducing unintended scrolling when document changes occur above the current scrollport. This is enabled by default where supported.

modern.name: revert-rule
modern.description: The revert-rule CSS keyword resets a property to its previous value in the cascade, as if the current style rule had not been present. It's especially useful with conditionals, to cancel a declaration when the condition is not met.

modern.name: stretch
modern.description: The stretch CSS keyword expands a box as needed to fit its contents until the maximum size is reached, without preserving the content's preferred aspect ratio.

modern.name: text-autospace
modern.description: The text-autospace CSS property sets whether and how to insert spaces in inter-script text (such as when mixing Latin and Chinese characters) and around punctuation.

modern.name: scroll-axis-lock
modern.description: The scroll-axis-lock property controls whether scrolling is locked to one dimension at a time or freely follows movement in two dimensions. By default, browsers may lock the scroll axis, ignoring minor perpendicular scrolling, when scrolling is nearly vertical or horizontal.

modern.name: attr()
modern.description: The attr() CSS function, in the context of any property, returns the value of an attribute of an HTML element, with the option to return it as a specific type or unit. You can set a default value for missing or invalid attributes.

modern.name: font-width
modern.description: The font-width CSS property selects a font face from a font family based on width, either by a keyword such as condensed or a percentage.

modern.name: progress()
modern.description: The progress() CSS function returns a ratio for the relative position of one value between two other values, clamped between 0 and 1. You can use it to interpolate a value for other calculations.

modern.name: window-drag
modern.description: The window-drag: move CSS declaration sets an element as a window drag handle, like a device's app title bar. You can use this to add click-and-drag areas to an installed progressive web app, often alongside window controls overlay.

modern.name: sibling-count() and sibling-index()
modern.description: The sibling-count() and sibling-index() CSS functions return integers that are useful to style elements based on their positions among siblings or on the number of siblings, for example as part of a calc() expression.

modern.name: text-box
modern.description: The text-box CSS property sets the spacing above and below text based on a font's typographic features. For example, text-box: trim-both ex alphabetic trims the top to the top of the letter x and the bottom to the bottom of most letters, without descenders.

modern.name: ruby-overhang
modern.description: The ruby-overhang CSS property sets whether ruby annotations may overlap adjacent text.

modern.name: alignment-baseline
modern.description: The alignment-baseline CSS property sets which baseline of an element is aligned with the corresponding baseline of its parent.

modern.name: Picture-in-picture (video)
modern.description: The picture-in-picture API allow websites to create a floating, always-on-top video window. Also known as PiP or pop-out video.

modern.name: background-clip: border-area
modern.description: The background-clip: border-area CSS declaration draws the background underneath only the border of an element.

modern.name: cross-origin() for url()
modern.description: The url() CSS function accepts a cross-origin() modifier to control cross-origin resource sharing (CORS) when requesting the URL. For example, url("https://example.com" cross-origin(anonymous))) does not send credentials to the URL.

modern.name: flex-wrap: balance
modern.description: The flex-wrap: balance CSS declaration distributes items in a multi-line flex container such that each line has about the same number of items.

modern.name: integrity() for url()
modern.description: The url() CSS function accepts an integrity() modifier to use subresource integrity to verify the response from the requested URL.

modern.name: named-feature()
modern.description: The named-feature() function, when used with @supports, checks if a named CSS behavior is supported. The CSS behavior names are defined by specification. For example, @supports named-feature(anchor-position-follows-transforms) checks whether anchor-positioning applies after transforms."

modern.name: referrer-policy() for url()
modern.description: The url() CSS function accepts a referrer-policy() modifier to choose which referrer to send when requesting the URL. For example, `url("https://example.com" referrer-policy(no-referrer)) does not send a referrer to the URL.

modern.name: text-fit
modern.description: The text-fit CSS property scales text to fill the inline size of its container. You can use this to grow or shrink headlines, captions, or pull quotes to fit a container.

modern.name: field-sizing
modern.description: The field-sizing CSS property allows form controls such as <textarea> to be sized based on their content.

modern.name: AccentColor and AccentColorText
modern.description: The AccentColor and AccentColorText CSS system color values are the background color and text color of accented user interface controls. To prevent browser fingerprinting, browsers may (and often do) use fixed color values that do not reflect user customization or theming choices.

modern.name: CSSPseudoElement
modern.description: A CSSPseudoElement object represents a pseudo-element and its context in the document tree. You get an instance through the pseudo() method of Element or CSSPseudoElement objects or the pseudoTarget property of some events.

modern.name: Gap decorations
modern.description: The column-rule and row-rule CSS properties display decorative lines between columns and rows of a flex, grid, or multi-column layout. The rule-break, rule-outset, and rule-paint-order properties control the appearance of these lines.

modern.name: Interest invokers
modern.description: Interest invokers, registered by the interestfor HTML attribute, trigger events and actions on a target element when a user shows interest in the element, through behaviors such as hover, focus, or long-press. Pseudo-elements apply styles to sources and targets of interest.

modern.name: Container style queries
modern.description: Container style queries with the @container at-rule apply styles to an element based on the values of custom properties of its container.

modern.name: Fullscreen API
modern.description: The fullscreen API makes a specific element fill the whole screen and hides most browser UI.

modern.name: Range syntax for style queries
modern.description: The @container style() CSS at-rule and if(style()) CSS function queries accept a range syntax, such as >, <, >=, <=, to query for inexact values.

modern.name: :open
modern.description: The :open CSS pseudo-class matches elements that have open states, like <details>, <dialog>, or <select>, based on their state.

modern.name: Hanging punctuation
modern.description: The hanging-punctuation CSS property puts punctuation characters outside of the box to align the text with the rest of the document.

modern.name: crisp-edges
modern.description: The image-rendering: crisp-edges CSS declaration scales images to preserve lines without blurring.

modern.name: Name-only container queries
modern.description: Name-only container queries with the @container … at-rule apply styles to an element based on the name of the element's container alone.

modern.name: text-decoration-skip-ink: all
modern.description: The text-decoration-skip-ink: all CSS declaration forces interruptions in underlines and overlines where the line would cross a glyph. This contrasts with auto, which does not skip for CJK glyphs.

modern.name: Media element pseudo-classes
modern.description: The :playing, :paused, :seeking, :buffering, :stalled, :muted, and :volume-locked CSS pseudo-classes match <audio> and <video> elements based on their state.

modern.name: overscroll-behavior
modern.description: The overscroll-behavior CSS property disables default scrolling behaviors when the edges of a scrolling area are reached.

modern.name: contrast-color()
modern.description: The contrast-color() CSS function picks a color that has guaranteed contrast against a specified foreground or background color.

modern.name: border-shape
modern.description: The border-shape CSS property sets the geometry of the border box, changing the shape of any applicable border, border image, focus outline, or shadow.

modern.name: Element-scoped view transitions
modern.description: The startViewTransition() method of an Element object starts a view transition that affects only that element's DOM tree. You can use this to run separate elements' transitions concurrently.

modern.name: @scope
modern.description: The @scope CSS at-rule sets the scope for a group of rules.

modern.name: baseline-shift
modern.description: The baseline-shift CSS property sets the position of an element relative to its dominant baseline.

modern.name: Custom highlights
modern.description: Custom highlights style arbitrary text ranges, without adding extra elements to the DOM.

modern.name: Grid lanes
modern.description: The display: grid-lanes and display: inline-grid-lanes CSS declarations create a layout where items are tightly packed in parallel lanes. Items are placed one by one in the lane that has the most available space. Also known as masonry.

modern.name: Math font family
modern.description: The font-family: math CSS declaration uses the browser default font face for displaying mathematical expressions.

modern.name: text-indent: each-line
modern.description: The text-indent: each-line CSS declaration indents text after forced breaks as well as to the first line of a block.

modern.name: text-indent: hanging
modern.description: The text-indent: hanging CSS declaration indents all lines except the first.

modern.name: Scroll-triggered animations
modern.description: Scroll-triggered animations start and stop CSS animations when an element is within or outside a scrolling range. It's an alternative to applying styles with the IntersectionObserver API. Not to be confused with scroll-driven animations.

modern.name: overflow-clip-margin
modern.description: The overflow-clip-margin CSS property sets how far overflow content may appear outside the bounds of an element before it's clipped by effects such as overflow: clip.

modern.name: shape()
modern.description: The shape() CSS function creates shapes with a series of commands like line, move, and curve. It can be used with clip-path and shape-outside.

modern.name: column-wrap
modern.description: The column-wrap and column-height CSS properties control when columns in a multicolumn layout wrap or overflow. You can use this to constrain the height of columns within a taller box or to create two-dimensional column layouts.

modern.name: text-justify
modern.description: The text-justify CSS property sets the justification method of text when text-align: justify is set.

modern.name: Active view transition
modern.description: The :active-view-transition CSS pseudo-class matches the root element when a view transition is active. The :active-view-transition-type() CSS pseudo-class matches only when the active view transition was started with the specified type.

modern.name: caret-shape
modern.description: The caret-shape CSS property sets the shape of the insertion caret, the symbol that shows where the next character is to be inserted or deleted.

modern.name: Container scroll-state queries
modern.description: Container scroll-state queries with the @container scroll-state(...) at-rule apply styles to an element based on the sticky positioning, snapped, scrollable, and scrolled state of the container.

modern.name: rcap unit
modern.description: The rcap CSS length unit is a font-relative length equal to the value of the cap unit on the root element. Cap-height is approximately equal to the height of a capital Latin letter.

modern.name: rch unit
modern.description: The rch CSS length unit is a font-relative length equal to the value of the ch unit on the root element. ch length is based on the width of the zero (0) character.

modern.name: rex unit
modern.description: The rex CSS length unit is a font-relative length that is equal to the x-height of the root element.

modern.name: ric unit
modern.description: The ric CSS length unit, or root international character, is a font-relative length equal to the width of CJK character relative to the root element.

modern.name: accent-color
modern.description: The accent-color CSS property sets a color for checkboxes, radio buttons, and other form controls.

modern.name: scrollbar-color
modern.description: The scrollbar-color CSS property sets the color of the scrollbar track and thumb.

modern.name: Spelling and grammar text decorations
modern.description: The text-decoration-line: spelling-error and text-decoration-line: grammar-error CSS declarations apply the browser's marking for spelling and grammatical mistakes. This is typically a wavy underline in red or green.

modern.name: Anchor position container queries
modern.description: Anchor position container queries with the @container anchored(fallback: …) at-rule apply styles to an element based on the element's anchor position.

modern.name: font-language-override
modern.description: The font-language-override CSS property sets which language-specific glyphs are displayed.

modern.name: Scroll marker target pseudo-classes
modern.description: The :target-current CSS pseudo-class selects the active scroll marker (as in ::scroll-marker), while the :target-after and :target-before pseudo-classes select the inactive markers preceding and following the active scroll marker.

modern.name: View transitions
modern.description: View transitions allow you to create animated visual transitions between different states of a document.

modern.name: view-transition-class
modern.description: The view-transition-class CSS property sets a name that can be used to apply styles to multiple named view transition pseudo-elements.

modern.name: ::details-content
modern.description: The ::details-content pseudo-element selects the expandable content of a <details> element, excluding the <summary>.

modern.name: Anchor positioning animations and transitions
modern.description: The anchor() and anchor-size() CSS functions animate or transition on changes such as the anchor box moving or the anchor element changing.

modern.name: content-visibility
modern.description: The content-visibility CSS property delays rendering an element, including layout and painting, until it is needed.

modern.name: dynamic-range-limit
modern.description: The dynamic-range-limit CSS property controls the peak luminance of high dynamic range content. You can use this to coordinate the apparent brightness of HDR and SDR content.

modern.name: text-wrap: pretty
modern.description: The text-wrap: pretty CSS declaration prioritizes better layout over speed when text is broken into multiple lines.

modern.name: scroll-target-group
modern.description: The scroll-target-group CSS property sets the container where anchor links act as scroll markers. Using selectors such as :target-current, you can style elements when a target has scrolled into view. It's an alternative to the ::scroll-marker-group pseudo-element, which generates scroll markers.

modern.name: @function
modern.description: The @function CSS at-rule defines a custom function that takes CSS values or custom properties as arguments, and returns a CSS value. It can be based on conditional logic such as by using the @media at-rule.

modern.name: corner-shape
modern.description: The corner-shape CSS property sets the shape of an element's corners when using border-radius, allowing for shapes other than rounded corners. For example, corner-shape: squircle is a shape in between a square and rounded corner.

modern.name: font-variant-emoji
modern.description: The font-variant-emoji CSS property sets the default presentation for emoji characters.

modern.name: abs() and sign()
modern.description: The abs() and sign() CSS functions compute the absolute value or the sign of the input.

modern.name: Viewport segments
modern.description: The viewport segment CSS environment variables and media features, and the viewport.segments API, allow you to adapt your layout to devices where the display is split, such as on foldable devices.

modern.name: if()
modern.description: The if() CSS function is an inline conditional value that returns a value based on a set of conditions.

modern.name: reading-flow
modern.description: The reading-flow CSS property sets the order in which flex or grid elements are rendered to speech or reached via focus navigation. The reading-order property overrides this order.

modern.name: print-color-adjust
modern.description: The print-color-adjust CSS property sets whether styles of printed pages should be adjusted to use less ink, in cases such as light text on a dark background.

modern.name: ::column
modern.description: The ::column CSS pseudo-element represents the individual columns of a multi-column layout container. Columns can only be styled with scroll snap CSS properties and can also have a ::scroll-marker pseudo-element, which scrolls to the column when activated.

modern.name: ::scroll-button
modern.description: The ::scroll-button(<dir>) CSS pseudo-element is a focusable button which scrolls its originating scroll container element in the specified direction.

modern.name: Hyphenate limit chars
modern.description: The hyphenate-limit-chars CSS property sets the number of characters in a word before it is hyphenated and the minimum number of characters on either side of the hyphen.

modern.name: interactivity
modern.description: The interactivity: inert CSS declaration makes an element and its descendants inert, like when using the inert HTML attribute. Inert elements can't be focused or clicked, their text can't be selected or found using the browser's find-in-page feature.

modern.name: Scroll markers
modern.description: A scroll marker scrolls a container to a scroll target. The ::scroll-marker CSS pseudo-element selects a scroll marker in a ::scroll-marker-group pseudo-element, generated before or after the scroll container. You can use them to navigate and style tables of contents, tab panels, and carousels.

modern.name: :has-slotted
modern.description: The :has-slotted CSS pseudo-class matches <slot> elements where the fallback content is not shown. The pseudo-class matches any slotted content, including white space, text nodes, or elements.

modern.name: paint()
modern.description: The paint() CSS function creates a custom image, drawn using a paint worklet, for an element's background or border.

modern.name: scroll-initial-target
modern.description: The scroll-initial-target: nearest CSS declaration sets the initial scroll position of its scroll container to the top of the element, much like scrolling to a URL fragment.

modern.name: Popover
modern.description: The popover HTML attribute creates an overlay to display content on top of other page content. Popovers can be shown declaratively using HTML, or using the showPopover() method.

modern.name: Device posture
modern.description: The device posture API and the device-posture CSS media feature reflect the physical posture of a device, such as whether a foldable device is folded or unfolded.

modern.name: ::target-text
modern.description: The ::target-text pseudo-element allows you to style text highlighted by a URL text fragment such as #:~:text=snippet.

modern.name: Cross-document view transitions
modern.description: The @view-transition CSS rule sets whether a document opts-in to transitions between documents in a multi-page application. Both the old and new document must opt-in for a transition to be triggered.

modern.name: Page setup
modern.description: The @page CSS at-rule sets the page-specific dimensions and margins for content such as printed documents, ebooks, or slides.

modern.name: ruby-align
modern.description: The ruby-align CSS property sets the spacing and alignment of ruby annotation text when it does not fill its available space.

modern.name: ruby-position
modern.description: The ruby-position CSS property sets the position of a ruby annotation in relation to its base text. Annotations can display over, under, or interleaved with the base text.

modern.name: scrollbar-gutter
modern.description: The scrollbar-gutter CSS property reserves space for the scrollbar, preventing unwanted layout changes as the scrollbar appears and disappears.

modern.name: scrollbar-width
modern.description: The scrollbar-width CSS property sets the width of the scrollbar.

modern.name: text-wrap
modern.description: The text-wrap CSS property sets how lines break in text that overflows the container. It is a shorthand for text-wrap-style and text-wrap-mode.

modern.name: box-decoration-break
modern.description: The box-decoration-break CSS property sets whether box decorations, such as borders or backgrounds, of an element divided across a page, column, or region wraps each fragment or splits across the break.

modern.name: justify-self in block layouts
modern.description: The justify-self CSS property aligns an item along a container's inline axis in block layouts, like it does in grid layouts. Likewise, the justify-items property sets a default justify-self value for all items in a container in a block layout.

modern.name: calc-size()
modern.description: The calc-size() CSS function computes mathematical expressions that include height and width keyword values, for example calc-size(fit-content, size / 2). Not to be confused with the calc() CSS function, which cannot use keyword values.

modern.name: interpolate-size
modern.description: The interpolate-size CSS property sets whether animations and transitions interpolate between a numeric value and a keyword value, such as from a fixed length to auto or fit-content.

modern.name: backdrop-filter
modern.description: The backdrop-filter CSS property applies graphical effects such as blurring or color shifting to the area behind an element.

modern.name: display animation
modern.description: You can animate elements between display: none and any other display value or animate between content-visibility: hidden and any other content-visibility value. This also applies to transitions.

modern.name: Relative colors
modern.description: The from keyword for color functions (color(), hsl(), oklch(), etc.) creates a new color based on a given color by modifying the values of the input color. Also known as relative color syntax (RCS).

modern.name: @starting-style
modern.description: The @starting-style CSS at-rule sets the starting values for properties that are transitioning when the target element's style is first updated.

modern.name: transition-behavior
modern.description: The transition-behavior: allow-discrete CSS declaration allows transitions for properties whose animation behavior is discrete. Such properties can't be interpolated and swap from their start value to the end value at 50%.

modern.name: font-size-adjust
modern.description: The font-size-adjust CSS property preserves apparent text size, regardless of the font used, by scaling fonts to the same size with respect to a specific metric, such as x-height. This can help make fallback fonts look the same size.

modern.name: Alt text for generated content
modern.description: The / notation in content CSS property values adds alternative text to generated content. For example, the content: url('upvote-icon.svg') / 'Upvote' declaration adds accessible 'Upvote' text to the SVG icon. Also known as alternate text.

modern.name: Registered custom properties
modern.description: The CSS.registerProperty() static method and the @property CSS at-rule register custom properties for which types and behaviors can be defined.

modern.name: Gradient interpolation
modern.description: Gradient interpolation controls how the colors between gradient stops are calculated in CSS. For example, linear-gradient(to right in oklch longer hue, red, red); calculates in the oklch color space, with the hue going all the way around the hue circle from red back to red.

modern.name: :state()
modern.description: The :state() CSS pseudo-class matches custom elements based on their custom state, set through the ElementInternals.states API.

modern.name: round(), mod(), and rem()
modern.description: The round(), mod(), and rem() CSS functions compute rounded values and the remainder after division.

modern.name: zoom
modern.description: The zoom CSS property scales the size of an element. Unlike the transform property, a zoomed element affects page layout.

modern.name: light-dark()
modern.description: The light-dark() CSS function accepts two colors and uses one depending on the current color scheme.

modern.name: text-wrap: balance
modern.description: The text-wrap: balance CSS declaration balances the length of each line when text is broken into multiple lines. Also known as headline balancing.

modern.name: Vertical form controls
modern.description: The writing-mode CSS property orients form elements (such as radio buttons, progress bars, or select menus) vertically when the writing mode is vertical-lr or vertical-rl. The direction CSS property sets whether inputs flow from top to bottom or bottom to top.

modern.name: align-content in block layouts
modern.description: The align-content property vertically aligns content in block layouts, like it does in flex or grid layouts.

modern.name: transform-box
modern.description: The transform-box CSS property sets the position and dimensions of the reference box relative to which an element's transformations are calculated.

modern.name: paint-order
modern.description: The paint-order CSS property sets the z-order of strokes, fills, and (in SVG content) markers. For example, paint-order: markers stroke fill; draws the markers, then stroke on top of markers, then fill on top of both markers and stroke.

modern.name: text-spacing-trim
modern.description: The text-spacing-trim CSS property controls spacing around CJK characters, avoiding excessive whitespace when using full-width punctuation characters.

modern.name: white-space-collapse
modern.description: The white-space-collapse CSS property sets whether new line characters are shown as line breaks, and whether multiple consecutive spaces are all displayed or combined.

modern.name: ::spelling-error and ::grammar-error
modern.description: The ::spelling-error and ::grammar-error CSS pseudo-elements match text that is highlighted as misspelled and grammatically incorrect, respectively.

modern.name: display: ruby
modern.description: The display: ruby CSS declaration renders an element with the box layout of a <ruby> HTML element. Child elements may use equivalents to <ruby> internal elements such as display: ruby-base for <rb>.

modern.name: font-palette animation
modern.description: You can animate color fonts between two font-palette values.

modern.name: page-orientation
modern.description: The page-orientation CSS property sets the rotation of a page after pagination. This allows pages with the same size declaration to display with different orientations.

modern.name: rect() and xywh()
modern.description: The rect() CSS function creates a rectangle shape with insets from the edges of an element. The xywh() CSS function creates a rectangle shifted by an x and y distance. They can be used with clip-path and shape-outside.

modern.name: :has()
modern.description: The :has() CSS functional pseudo-class matches an element if any of the selectors passed as parameters would match at least one element.

modern.name: cap unit
modern.description: The cap CSS length unit corresponds to the height of Latin capital letters.

modern.name: counter-set
modern.description: The counter-set CSS property creates (and optionally sets a value for) a counter, the numbers for a series of headings or ordered list items.

modern.name: linear() easing
modern.description: The linear() easing function for animations and transitions interpolates linearly between the control points, and can be used to approximate complex easing functions, such as a bounce effect.

modern.name: mask-border
modern.description: The mask-border CSS property sets how the edges of an element are masked. It is a shorthand for mask-border-outset, mask-border-repeat, mask-border-slice, mask-border-source, and mask-border-width.

modern.name: Nesting
modern.description: CSS nesting allows for shorter selectors, easier reading, and more modularity by nesting rules inside others.

modern.name: Numeric factory functions
modern.description: The numeric factory functions, such as CSS.px() or CSS.kHz(), return a CSSUnitValue representing a CSS number value (as in 12px or 440kHz).

modern.name: :dir()
modern.description: The :dir() CSS functional pseudo-class matches elements by text direction, either right to left (rtl) or left to right (ltr).

modern.name: Exponential functions (CSS)
modern.description: The pow(), sqrt(), hypot(), log(), and exp() CSS functions compute various exponential functions.

modern.name: Masks
modern.description: The mask CSS property (and several longhand properties) partially or completely hides an element according to the shape and depth of an image.

modern.name: scripting media query
modern.description: The scripting CSS media query sets styles based on whether scripting such as JavaScript is available. Values are enabled if scripting is available, initial-only if scripting is only available on page load (for example, printed content), or none.

modern.name: background-clip: text
modern.description: The background-clip: text CSS declaration draws the background underneath only the text in the element.

modern.name: lh unit
modern.description: The lh CSS length unit corresponds to the requested line height, the computed value of the line-height property. Some lines may be higher than this based on their content.

modern.name: rlh unit
modern.description: The rlh CSS length unit is a font-relative length relative to the line height of root element.

modern.name: :user-valid and :user-invalid
modern.description: The :user-valid and :user-invalid pseudo-classes match form controls that have been marked as valid or invalid based on their validation constraints.

modern.name: Clip path boxes
modern.description: The fill-box, stroke-box, and view-box values for clip-path set an edge of the element's box to use as the clipping shape.

modern.name: prefers-reduced-transparency media query
modern.description: The prefers-reduced-transparency CSS media query sets styles based on whether the user prefers to reduce the amount of transparent effects on their device, for example to improve contrast and legibility.

modern.name: word-break: auto-phrase
modern.description: The word-break: auto-phrase CSS declaration specifies that wrapping should occur at natural phrase boundaries, especially in CJK languages.

modern.name: resize (CSS property)
modern.description: The resize CSS property sets whether an element can be resized by the user, and on which axes.

modern.name: font-synthesis-position
modern.description: The font-synthesis-position CSS property sets whether or not the browser should synthesize subscript and superscript typefaces when they're missing from the font.

modern.name: @counter-style
modern.description: The @counter-style CSS at-rule sets custom counter styles for list items. For example, you can use a sequence of specific symbols instead of numbers for an ordered list.

modern.name: contain-intrinsic-size
modern.description: The contain-intrinsic-size CSS property sets the intrinsic size of an element. When using size containment, the browser will lay out the element as if it had a single child of this size.

modern.name: Hyphenate character
modern.description: The hyphenate-character CSS property sets the character or string to use at the end of a line before a line break.

modern.name: Hyphenation
modern.description: The hyphens CSS property controls when long words are broken by line wrapping. Although called hyphens, the property applies to word-splitting behavior across languages, such as customary spelling changes or the use of other characters. Support for non-English languages varies significantly.

modern.name: image-set()
modern.description: The image-set() CSS function provides a set of images at different resolutions or pixel densities, which the browser can pick from, depending on the device capabilities.

modern.name: Overflow media queries
modern.description: The overflow-block and overflow-inline CSS media queries set styles based on the way a device displays content that's larger than the viewport or page area. For example, a laptop lets users scroll to reveal content, while a printer displays overflowing content on additional pages.

modern.name: Update frequency media query
modern.description: The update CSS media query sets styles based on whether and how fast the user's device can modify display after it has been rendered. For example, you can avoid animations on devices that aren't fast enough to display them smoothly.

modern.name: Subgrid
modern.description: The subgrid value for the grid-template-columns and grid-template-rows properties allows a grid item to inherit the grid definition of its parent grid container.

modern.name: font-variant-position
modern.description: The font-variant-position CSS property sets whether to use alternate glyphs for subscript and superscript text.

modern.name: overlay
modern.description: The overlay CSS property, used as an allow-discrete CSS transition, prevents a top layer element, such as a popover or a <dialog>, from being removed from the top layer before it has finished animating. You can't set the value of the overlay property; only use it as transition property.

modern.name: Page selectors
modern.description: The :first, :left, and :right pseudo-classes select pages based on their position in sequence after pagination.

modern.name: Two-value display property
modern.description: The display CSS property accepts multiple keyword values, such as inline flex or block flow, to explicitly set an element's inner and outer layout mode. Also known as 2-value, multi-keyword, or multiple value syntax.

modern.name: animation-composition
modern.description: The animation-composition CSS property chooses how to combine animations that affect the same property.

modern.name: baseline-source
modern.description: The baseline-source CSS property controls how inline-level boxes with multiple lines of text are aligned with the surrounding text. By default, which typographic baseline is used depends on the display property value.

modern.name: calc() keywords
modern.description: The e, pi, infinity, and NaN keywords represent well-defined constants accepted in CSS math functions such as calc().

modern.name: :nth-child() of <selector>
modern.description: The of syntax for the :nth-child() and :nth-last-child() CSS functional pseudo-classes match elements by the relative position of elements, counted from the first or last sibling matching a selector list.

modern.name: color-mix()
modern.description: The color-mix() function mixes two colors in a given color space and by a given amount. Commonly, lighter or darker variations of a color are created by mixing with white or black.

modern.name: color()
modern.description: The color() function picks a color from a given color space. Wide gamut color spaces like display-p3 allow showing more vibrant and saturated colors than the standard srgb color space.

modern.name: Lab and LCH
modern.description: The CIE Lab color space expresses colors in terms of lightness and how red/green and blue/yellow a color is. LCH is a variant of Lab with polar coordinates. These color spaces can be used with the CSS color(), lab(), and lch() functions. Also known as CIELAB and CIELCH.

modern.name: Oklab and OkLCh
modern.description: The Oklab color space expresses colors in terms of lightness and how red/green and blue/yellow a color is, aiming to match how humans perceive colors. OkLCh is a variant of Oklab with polar coordinates. These color spaces can be used with the CSS oklab() and oklch() functions.

modern.name: CSS typed object model
modern.description: The CSSStyleValue and its subclasses represent CSS values as distinct types instead of only strings. Also known as typed OM.

modern.name: font-synthesis-small-caps
modern.description: The font-synthesis-small-caps CSS property sets whether or not the browser should synthesize small caps typefaces when they're missing from the font.

modern.name: font-synthesis-style
modern.description: The font-synthesis-style CSS property sets whether or not the browser should synthesize italic and oblique typefaces when they're missing from the font.

modern.name: font-synthesis-weight
modern.description: The font-synthesis-weight CSS property sets whether or not the browser should synthesize bold typefaces when they're missing from the font.

modern.name: Media query range syntax
modern.description: The range syntax of CSS media queries allows you to use mathematical comparison operators such as <, >, <=, and >= to define a range of values for a media query. For example, (400px < width < 1000px) returns true if the viewport width is between 400px and 1000px.

modern.name: outline
modern.description: The outline CSS shorthand sets the color, style, and width of a line around an element, outside of the border.

modern.name: font-variant-alternates
modern.description: The font-variant-alternates CSS property, along with the @font-feature-values at-rule, chooses when to use a font's alternate glyphs.

modern.name: Trigonometric functions (CSS)
modern.description: The sin(), cos(), tan(), asin(), acos(), atan(), and atan2() CSS functions compute various trigonometric functions.

modern.name: color-gamut media query
modern.description: The color-gamut media query sets styles based on the colors a device can display.

modern.name: Container queries (size)
modern.description: Container size queries with the @container (…) at-rule apply styles to an element based on a dimension of its container, such as width or height.

modern.name: :autofill
modern.description: The :autofill pseudo-class matches <input> elements that have been filled in automatically by the browser.

modern.name: initial-letter
modern.description: The initial-letter CSS property sets the number of lines the first letter of an element occupies. You can use the property to make a raised capital or drop cap.

modern.name: MathML
modern.description: MathML, or the Mathematical Markup Language, describes mathematical notation, such as expressions and formulas. Also known as MathML Core.
